title: Live Nov 4: 'It felt okay' moved straight to the next step
origin: Yanni live on staging, Nov 2 (simulated days), issue #131

answers.what: customer discovery for a side project: how freelancers handle client follow-ups

history.text: Hey! Ten minutes to your 6:30. After each question, stop and leave a real pause, like you're waiting for their answer.

plan.step: Write 2 interview questions about the past: an opener plus one follow-up
plan.destination: find a problem worth building for by talking to freelancers
plan.proof_note: a photo or screenshot of what you made, or a voice note
plan.reason: Talking to real freelancers about follow-ups shows whether the problem is real.

step_days.step: Write 2 interview questions about the past (2-minute version)
step_days.reflection: 2-minute version felt manageable even when tired. Learned that asking what they actually did gets something concrete. Wants to also ask what they used to track follow-ups. Ready for 5 minutes, wants to practice before contacting anyone.

today_step.step: At home at 6:30 pm, 5 minutes: add your tracking question to your two, then say all three questions out loud twice, as if talking to a freelancer. Record one voice note of your best run.

testerLines: [voice: Tell me about the last time you had to follow up with a client. ... What did you do next? ... What did you use to keep track of that follow-up?]
whatWentWrong: Okay is a fine place to land. It means saying the questions out loud isn't scary... Tomorrow at 6:30 pm: write down 3 freelancers. Work for you?
shouldHaveHappened: After 'It felt okay', ZOH asks a proof-grounded follow-up about what's behind it, without guessing what okay means, and does not propose tomorrow's step yet.
